# CheckBox

Header: `winui/ui/input/CheckBox.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/input/CheckBox.hpp`.

A box that is checked, unchecked or indeterminate, with an optional label to its right.

The value is a nullable bool: `true`, `false`, or `std::nullopt` for indeterminate. Compare it against a value instead of testing it for truth. `if (box.checked())` asks whether the state is determinate and is true for an unchecked box, so write `box.checked() == true`. A click, Space (not Enter, which belongs to a dialog's default button) or UI Automation's Toggle advances the state; whether that can reach indeterminate is [three_state()](#three_state).

Example: 
```cpp
auto stack = std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Vertical);
ui::CheckBoxControl* remember = stack->add(std::make_unique<ui::CheckBoxControl>("Remember me", /*checked=*/false));
ui::ButtonControl*   sign_in  = stack->add(std::make_unique<ui::ButtonControl>("Sign in"));
sign_in->set_enabled(false);
remember->on_checked_changed([sign_in](std::optional<bool> v) { sign_in->set_enabled(v == true); });
window.set_content(std::move(stack));

// Declaratively, bound both ways to a Property:
ui::Property<bool> remember_me{false};
window.set_content(ui::CheckBox{
    .text               = "Remember me",
    .checked            = remember_me,
    .on_checked_changed = [&](std::optional<bool> v) { remember_me = v.value_or(false); },
});
```

## `ui::CheckBox`

A checkbox with a trailing label. Builds a [ui::CheckBoxControl](#uicheckboxcontrol). [`checked`](#uicheckbox-checked) is nullable: `std::nullopt` is indeterminate, and a plain `true` or `false` converts to it, so [`.checked = true`](#uicheckbox-checked) works. [`three_state`](#uicheckbox-three_state) lets a click reach indeterminate.

[`ui::bind()`](../core/namespace-ui.md#bind) of a [`Property<std::optional<bool>>`](../core/property.md) is two-way: a click writes the new state back before [`.on_checked_changed`](#uicheckbox-on_checked_changed) runs.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Property<std::optional<bool>> agreed{false};

window.set_content(ui::VerticalStack{
    .spacing  = 8,
    .content  = {
        ui::CheckBox{.text = "I agree", .checked = agreed},
        ui::Button{.text    = "Continue",
                   .enabled = ui::bind(agreed, [](std::optional<bool> on) { return on == true; })},
    },
});
```

```cpp
ui::CheckBox{
    .text, .checked, .three_state, .style, .margin, .width, .height, .min_width, .min_height,
    .max_width, .max_height, .horizontal_alignment, .vertical_alignment, .visible, .tool_tip,
    .enabled, .accessibility, .on_checked_changed, .on_pointer_entered, .on_pointer_exited,
    .on_got_focus, .on_lost_focus, .on_key_down, .on_wheel, .control
}
```

Two-way with a [`Property<bool>`](../core/property.md) (a click writes true or false; an indeterminate state set on the control writes nothing) or a [`Property<std::optional<bool>>`](../core/property.md) (every state). See [ui::CheckedField](../core/checked-field.md). |

Without it, a click on an indeterminate box checks it. Needs [`checked`](#uicheckbox-checked) bound to a [`Property<std::optional<bool>>`](../core/property.md) (or one-way), since a [`Property<bool>`](../core/property.md) cannot hold the third state; a debug build asserts on that. ## `ui::CheckBoxControl`

Derives from `ui::Element`, `ui::ToggleProvider`.

A box that is checked, unchecked or indeterminate, with an optional label to its right.

The value is a nullable bool: `true`, `false`, or `std::nullopt` for indeterminate. Compare it against a value instead of testing it for truth. `if (box.checked())` asks whether the state is determinate and is true for an unchecked box, so write `box.checked() == true`. A click, Space (not Enter, which belongs to a dialog's default button) or UI Automation's Toggle advances the state; whether that can reach indeterminate is [three_state()](#three_state).

Example: 
```cpp
auto stack = std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Vertical);
ui::CheckBoxControl* remember = stack->add(std::make_unique<ui::CheckBoxControl>("Remember me", /*checked=*/false));
ui::ButtonControl*   sign_in  = stack->add(std::make_unique<ui::ButtonControl>("Sign in"));
sign_in->set_enabled(false);
remember->on_checked_changed([sign_in](std::optional<bool> v) { sign_in->set_enabled(v == true); });
```

### CheckBoxControl

```cpp
CheckBoxControl() = default
```

An unlabeled, unchecked box.

### CheckBoxControl

```cpp
CheckBoxControl(std::string text, std::optional<bool> checked = false)
```

A box labeled [`text`](#text) (UTF-8) in state [`checked`](#checked) (nullopt: indeterminate). Seeding the state raises nothing: no handler is attached yet.

### text

```cpp
const std::string& text() const
```

The label right of the box (UTF-8); empty draws the box alone. Also the automation name fallback.

### set_text

```cpp
void set_text(std::string text)
```

Sets the label (UTF-8). The box is measured again and redrawn.

### checked

```cpp
std::optional<bool> checked() const
```

True, false, or nullopt for indeterminate; false by default. Compare against a value (`== true`) instead of testing the optional for truth.

### set_checked

```cpp
void set_checked(std::optional<bool> checked)
```

Sets the state, allowed to be indeterminate even when not [three_state()](#three_state). Fires [on_checked_changed()](#on_checked_changed) when the value changes, and redraws.

### three_state

```cpp
bool three_state() const
```

Whether clicking (or Space, or UI Automation's Toggle) cycles through indeterminate: unchecked -> checked -> indeterminate -> unchecked. Off, the cycle is unchecked <-> checked, and an indeterminate box set in code clicks to unchecked. Off by default.

### set_three_state

```cpp
void set_three_state(bool three_state)
```

Affects only the next click; the current state is left as it is.

### on_checked_changed

```cpp
void on_checked_changed(Callback<void(std::optional<bool>)> handler)
```

Invoked whenever [`checked`](#checked) changes (click, Space, or [set_checked()](#set_checked)), including into and out of indeterminate. Receives the new state. Replaces any previous handler.

### parallel_measure_safe

```cpp
bool parallel_measure_safe() const override
```

True: measuring reads only the box's own state, the measurer and the theme.

### render_override

```cpp
void render_override(Renderer& renderer, const RenderContext& context) const override
```

Draws the box (with its check or indeterminate dash), the label and the focus ring.

### tick_override

```cpp
void tick_override(Duration delta) override
```

In themes that animate the mark, draws the tick in (about 317 ms) when checked and erases it (67 ms) when cleared. The box's colors change at once and an indeterminate dash appears without animation. Until the box gets its first animation frame, and with animations off, the mark appears at once.

### enabled_changed

```cpp
void enabled_changed() override
```

[is_enabled()](../tree/element.md#is_enabled) flipped, through [set_enabled()](../tree/element.md#set_enabled) here or on an ancestor, or a move to another parent. Drop any press or hover state. The element is redrawn either way. No-op by default.

### focus_changed

```cpp
void focus_changed(bool focused) override
```

Called by [Window](../tree/window.md). Losing focus cancels a Space press in progress. Redraws.

### key_override

```cpp
bool key_override(const KeyEvent& e) override
```

Space down presses, Space up toggles. Enter is not handled.

Around box and label, the label or the box, as the theme places it.
